w: Oh, sad are winter nights, and slow; And sad's a song that's dumb; And sad it is to lie and know Another dawn will come.
All tenderly his messenger he chose; Deep-hearted, pure, with scented dew still wet-- One perfect rose.
Where their tender grasses heal Ancient scars of trench and tomb I shall never walk; nor kneel Where the bones of poets bloom.
Once when I was young and true, Someone left me sad-- Broke my brittle heart in two; And that is very bad.
The ladies men admire, I've heard, Would shudder at a wicked word.
Roam with young Persephone, Plucking poppies for your slumber...
She married an affluent millionaire So gallant and handsome and wise and gay, And rated in Bradstreet at Double A.
If there's one gone whistling by Would I let it grieve me?
Now you're casting yearning glances At the pale Penelope; Cutting in on Claudia's dances; Taking Iris out to tea.
I'd rise each day at rosy dawn And bustle gaily down; In evening's cool, you'd spray the lawn When you came back from town.
I shall tread, another year, Ways I walked with Grief, Past the dry, ungarnered ear And the brittle leaf.
My garden blossoms pink and white, A place of decorous murmuring Where I am safe from August night And cannot feel the knife of spring.
You shall have my further years,-- You shall walk with me to-morrow.
You will be frail and musty With peering, furtive head, Whilst I am young and lusty Among the roaring dead.
Where never I walked alone before I wander in the weeds; And people scream and bar the door, And rattle at their beads.
Other lads, their ways are daring: Other lads, they're not afraid; Other lads, they show they're caring; Other lads--they know a maid.

Tender though the love he bore, You had loved a little more....
Fine he was in the game he played-- Kissed, and promised, and threw me over, And rode away with a prettier maid.
Shall I bar the strolling guest, Bind my brow with willow, When, they say, the empty breast Is the softer pillow?

What if at night, beneath a sky of ashes, He should seek my doorstep, pale with need?
There's many to claw at a heart unclad, And little the wonder it ripped and tore.
Then Sorrow came to stay, And lay upon my breast; He walked with me in the day, And knew me best.
If I seek a lovelier part, Where I travel goes my heart; Where I stray my thought must go; With me wanders my desire.
I wore my heart like a wet, red stain On the breast of a velvet gown.
Lilacs blossom just as sweet Now my heart is shattered.
And I lie here warm, and I lie here dry, And watch the worms slip by, slip by.
But when, one day, a boy comes by And pleads me with your happiest vow, "There was a lad I knew--" I'll sigh; "I do not know him now."
